metadata.title: XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System (Chen & Guestrin, 2016)
metadata.framework: Scalable gradient tree boosting with regularization, sparsity-aware learning, and system-level optimizations
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on arXiv:1603.02754 PDF text.

nodes.name: Regularized tree boosting objective
nodes.statement: Given a dataset with $n$ examples and $m$ features, predict $\hat{y}_i = \sum_{k=1}^{K} f_k(\mathbf{x}_i)$ where each $f_k \in \mathcal{F}$ is a regression tree. The regularized objective is $\mathcal{L} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} l(y_i, \hat{y}_i) + \sum_{k=1}^{K} \Omega(f_k)$ where $\Omega(f) = \gamma T + \frac{1}{2} \lambda \|\mathbf{w}\|^2$, $T$ is the number of leaves, and $\mathbf{w}$ are the leaf weights.

nodes.name: Second-order Taylor expansion of loss
nodes.statement: At boosting round $t$, approximate the loss using a second-order Taylor expansion: $\mathcal{L}^{(t)} \approx \sum_{i=1}^{n} [l(y_i, \hat{y}_i^{(t-1)}) + g_i f_t(\mathbf{x}_i) + \frac{1}{2} h_i f_t(\mathbf{x}_i)^2] + \Omega(f_t)$, where $g_i = \partial_{\hat{y}^{(t-1)}} l(y_i, \hat{y}_i^{(t-1)})$ and $h_i = \partial^2_{\hat{y}^{(t-1)}} l(y_i, \hat{y}_i^{(t-1)})$ are the first and second derivatives of the loss.

nodes.name: Optimal leaf weights and split gain
nodes.statement: For a fixed tree structure $q$, the optimal weight for leaf $j$ is $w_j^* = -\frac{\sum_{i \in I_j} g_i}{\sum_{i \in I_j} h_i + \lambda}$ and the optimal objective value is $\tilde{\mathcal{L}} = -\frac{1}{2} \sum_{j=1}^{T} \frac{(\sum_{i \in I_j} g_i)^2}{\sum_{i \in I_j} h_i + \lambda} + \gamma T$, where $I_j$ is the set of instances in leaf $j$.

nodes.name: Split finding gain
nodes.statement: The gain from splitting a leaf into left ($I_L$) and right ($I_R$) is: $\mathrm{Gain} = \frac{1}{2} \left[ \frac{(\sum_{i \in I_L} g_i)^2}{\sum_{i \in I_L} h_i + \lambda} + \frac{(\sum_{i \in I_R} g_i)^2}{\sum_{i \in I_R} h_i + \lambda} - \frac{(\sum_{i \in I} g_i)^2}{\sum_{i \in I} h_i + \lambda} \right] - \gamma$. The term $\gamma$ acts as a pruning threshold: splits with negative gain are pruned.

nodes.name: Sparsity-aware split finding
nodes.statement: For each tree node, learn a default direction for missing values. During split finding, only route non-missing values and assign missing values to the default direction. The optimal default direction is found by trying both left and right and choosing the one with higher gain.

nodes.name: Exact greedy split finding
nodes.statement: For each node, enumerate all features; for each feature, sort instances by feature value and scan linearly to find the split with maximum gain using the gradient statistics $(g_i, h_i)$. Complexity: $O(Kd \cdot n \log n)$ for $K$ trees, $d$ features, $n$ examples.

nodes.name: Approximate split finding with weighted quantile sketch
nodes.statement: Instead of exact enumeration, propose candidate split points using percentiles of the feature distribution, weighted by the second-order gradient $h_i$. Map continuous features into buckets defined by these candidates and aggregate gradient statistics per bucket. A novel distributed weighted quantile sketch algorithm provides provable guarantees.

nodes.name: Column block and cache-aware access
nodes.statement: Data is stored in compressed column (CSC) format in in-memory blocks. For the exact algorithm, the block structure allows parallel split finding across features. For the approximate algorithm, cache-aware prefetching reduces cache misses during gradient accumulation.

nodes.name: Relationship to gradient boosting machine (GBM)
nodes.statement: XGBoost extends Friedman's gradient boosting by: (1) using a second-order Taylor expansion instead of first-order (Newton step), (2) adding explicit $L_1$ and $L_2$ regularization on leaf weights and tree complexity, (3) incorporating shrinkage (learning rate) and column subsampling, and (4) engineering for scalability.
